faqs.question: How do I convert a PDF to Word for free?
faqs.answer: Upload your PDF to this tool and click Convert. It extracts all text content and generates a Word-compatible .doc file you can download and edit in Microsoft Word, Google Docs, or LibreOffice.

faqs.question: Does this preserve PDF formatting?
faqs.answer: The tool extracts text content with basic paragraph structure. Complex layouts, tables, and images are converted to their text equivalents. For best results with heavily formatted PDFs, consider using desktop software.

faqs.question: Is my PDF uploaded to a server?
faqs.answer: No. The entire conversion happens in your browser using PDF.js. Your document never leaves your device — nothing is uploaded, nothing is stored.

faqs.question: Can I convert scanned PDFs?
faqs.answer: This tool works with text-based PDFs where text was typed or generated digitally. For scanned PDFs (which are images), you'll need OCR first — try our Image to Text tool to extract text from scanned pages.

faqs.question: What's the maximum PDF size?
faqs.answer: There's no hard limit since processing happens locally, but very large PDFs (100+ pages) may take longer and use more memory. For best performance, split large PDFs first using our PDF Splitter.

faqs.question: Can I convert password-protected PDFs?
faqs.answer: No. Password-protected PDFs must be unlocked before conversion. Remove the password using the original PDF software or your PDF viewer's security settings.

metadata.title: Claude Code Text Formatter
metadata.description: Clean up messy terminal & Claude Code output. Strip ANSI codes, line numbers, and control characters.

faqs.question: What does the Claude Code Text Formatter do?
faqs.answer: It cleans up messy terminal and Claude Code output by removing ANSI escape codes, line numbers, and control characters. The result is plain, readable text that you can copy, paste, and share without the noise.

faqs.question: Will my text be uploaded to a server?
faqs.answer: No. Everything runs locally in your browser. Your text never leaves your device, so it's safe for cleaning output that contains sensitive information.

faqs.question: What are ANSI escape codes?
faqs.answer: ANSI escape codes are special character sequences that terminals use to add colors and formatting. When you copy terminal output, these codes often appear as raw garbage sequences or invisible control characters. This tool strips them automatically.

faqs.question: Can I keep line numbers in the output?
faqs.answer: Line numbers are removed by default. If your output has no line numbers, or you only need to strip ANSI codes, you can turn the Strip Line Numbers option off before formatting.

intro.title: What Is the Claude Code Text Formatter?
paragraphs: The Claude Code Text Formatter cleans up messy terminal and Claude Code output by stripping ANSI escape codes, line numbers, and control characters. It turns cluttered CLI output into plain, readable text that you can copy, paste, and share without the noise.
Everything runs locally in your browser. Your input never leaves your device, so the tool is safe for cleaning output that contains sensitive information.

sections.title: How to Use It
paragraphs: Cleaning up output takes just a few seconds:
items: Paste or type your messy text into the Input box.
Choose which elements to strip: ANSI codes, control characters, and line numbers.
Click Format and copy the cleaned result from the Output box.

sections.title: Why Terminal Output Looks Messy
paragraphs: Terminal tools like Claude Code add ANSI escape codes to colorize text, highlight syntax, and control the cursor. When you copy that output into a plain-text editor, the escape codes are often shown as raw garbage sequences or invisible control characters that break your document.
Line numbers added by terminal multiplexers and log viewers also create extra noise. The formatter removes all of this automatically.

sections.title: Typical Use Cases
items: Cleaning Claude Code session logs before sharing them in bug reports.
Copying terminal output into tickets, docs, or chat messages without escape-code noise.
Preparing log snippets for code reviews and documentation.
Removing line numbers from code listings so they can be pasted back into editors.

sections.title: Tips
items: If a pasted block still looks odd, try toggling Strip Control to remove hidden characters.
The tool handles output from most modern terminals, including iTerm, Windows Terminal, and VS Code's integrated terminal.
There is no limit on input size, so you can clean very long logs in one pass.

faqs.question: How does the fancy text generator work?
faqs.answer: It converts your text into special Unicode characters that look like different fonts. These characters are part of the Unicode standard, so they work everywhere that supports Unicode — social media bios, messages, comments, and more.

faqs.question: Can I use fancy text on Instagram, TikTok, and Twitter?
faqs.answer: Yes. The generated text uses Unicode characters that work on Instagram bios and captions, TikTok bios, Twitter/X posts, Facebook, YouTube, Discord, and virtually any platform that supports text input.

faqs.question: Why do some characters look different on different devices?
faqs.answer: Unicode characters are rendered by each device's font system. Some older devices or browsers may not support all Unicode blocks, which can cause certain styles to display as boxes or question marks. The most widely supported styles are Bold, Italic, and Circled.

faqs.question: Is there a character limit?
faqs.answer: There is no limit in this tool. However, keep in mind that some Unicode characters count as 2-4 characters on platforms with character limits (like Twitter's 280 character limit), since they use multi-byte encoding.

faqs.question: Are these actual fonts?
faqs.answer: No — these are Unicode characters that visually resemble different font styles. Real fonts require CSS or font files. The advantage of Unicode text is that it can be pasted anywhere without any special formatting.

metadata.title: Image Compressor
metadata.description: Compress images by up to 90% with adjustable quality. No upload, runs in your browser.

faqs.question: Does the image compressor work in my browser?
faqs.answer: Yes. All compression runs locally in your browser using WebAssembly and the canvas API — PNG uses the oxipng quantizer, GIF uses gifsicle, AVIF uses libavif, and SVG uses svgo. Nothing is uploaded to a server, so your files stay on your device.

faqs.question: Which formats are supported?
faqs.answer: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, AVIF, and SVG. You can also change the output format while compressing, so a bulky PNG can become a small WebP, AVIF, or JPEG in one step.

faqs.question: How much can I reduce the file size?
faqs.answer: Photos typically compress 50% to 90% as JPEG, WebP, or AVIF. PNG and GIF files gain the most from the color-count and dithering controls, which can shrink them dramatically.

faqs.question: What do the Colors and Dithering options do?
faqs.answer: Colors sets the palette size for PNG and GIF output (2–256). Fewer colors mean smaller files but a flatter look. Dithering blends adjacent colors to hide banding when the palette is reduced.

faqs.question: Can I compress multiple images at once?
faqs.answer: Yes. Upload as many images as you like, compress them all at once, and download the results individually or as a single ZIP archive.

intro.title: What Is the Image Compressor?
paragraphs: The Image Compressor shrinks image file sizes by up to 90%. It supports JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, AVIF, and SVG, with batch upload, color-count and dithering controls, resizing, and ZIP download. PNG files are compressed with the oxipng quantizer, GIF with gifsicle, AVIF with libavif, and SVG with svgo.
All compression happens in your browser — the WebAssembly engines run in a background worker so the page stays responsive, nothing is uploaded, and your images never leave your device.

sections.title: How to Compress an Image
paragraphs: Compressing an image takes three steps:
items: Upload or drop one or more images.
Choose the output format, quality, colors, dithering, and resize options.
Click Compress All and watch the progress.
Compare sizes, then download each image or the whole batch as a ZIP.

sections.title: Which Format Should I Choose?
paragraphs: JPEG is the best all-around choice for photos. WebP and AVIF offer even better compression for photos and graphics and are supported by all modern browsers. PNG is lossless and ideal for sharp edges, text, or transparency — use the Colors and Dithering controls to shrink it dramatically. GIF suits small animations and logos with flat colors.

sections.title: Typical Use Cases
items: Shrinking product photos before uploading them to an online store.
Optimizing images for web pages and email newsletters to speed up loading.
Reducing file size so images fit within messenger and email attachment limits.
Preparing social media images that upload faster on slow connections.

sections.title: Tips
items: Start at 80% quality — it usually looks identical to the original while saving a lot of space.
For images with transparency, keep PNG and only lower quality if size still matters.
Compress the largest images first; they offer the biggest savings.
Use the format dropdown to convert a bulky PNG to WebP or JPEG in the same step.

faqs.question: How do I resize an image?
faqs.answer: Upload an image, then either pick a social media preset or enter a custom width and height in pixels. You can also scale by percentage. Maintain aspect ratio keeps the proportions intact so your image isn't stretched.

faqs.question: Which formats are supported?
faqs.answer: You can upload JPG, PNG, WebP, and other common image formats. The resized result is downloaded as a PNG by default, which preserves quality and transparency.

faqs.question: What are the social media presets for?
faqs.answer: Presets apply the exact pixel dimensions recommended for Instagram posts (1080x1080), stories (1080x1920), YouTube thumbnails (1280x720), Facebook covers, and more — so you don't have to look up the numbers yourself.

faqs.question: Will enlarging a small image make it blurry?
faqs.answer: Enlarging an image interpolates new pixels, so the result can look softer or blurry. For best quality, resize images that are already at least as large as the target dimensions.

intro.title: What Is the Image Resizer?
paragraphs: The Image Resizer lets you change the width and height of an image to exact pixel values, percentages, or popular social media presets. A live preview updates as you adjust the settings, so you can confirm the result before downloading.
All resizing happens in your browser. Images are never uploaded, which keeps the tool fast, free, and private.

sections.title: How to Resize an Image
items: Upload or drop an image.
Choose a social media preset, or enter width and height in pixels.
Keep Maintain aspect ratio on to avoid distortion, or turn it off for custom stretching.
Preview the result and download your resized PNG.

sections.title: Social Media Presets
paragraphs: The built-in presets cover the most commonly recommended dimensions: Instagram square posts (1080x1080), Instagram stories and Reels (1080x1920), YouTube thumbnails (1280x720), Facebook profile and cover sizes, Twitter/X header images, and Pinterest pins. Selecting a preset automatically fills in the exact width and height for you.

sections.title: Understanding Aspect Ratio
paragraphs: Aspect ratio is the relationship between an image's width and height. Changing only one dimension breaks the ratio and distorts the image. With Maintain aspect ratio enabled, the resizer scales both dimensions proportionally, and the Aspect Ratio Calculator is available if you need to work out dimensions for a specific ratio like 16:9 or 4:3.

sections.title: Tips
items: Resize before compressing for the smallest final file size.
Use 100% zoom in the preview to check sharpness after resizing.
For print, target at least 300 DPI at the final print size.
Downscaling improves perceived sharpness — it's a great way to clean up large camera photos.

faqs.question: Which image formats can I convert?
faqs.answer: The converter supports 20+ formats including JPG, PNG, WebP, SVG, HEIC, GIF, BMP, TIFF, and ICO. You can convert in any direction between the supported formats.

faqs.question: Does the conversion happen on my device?
faqs.answer: Yes. Conversion runs entirely in your browser using the canvas API. Your images are never uploaded to a server, which makes the tool fast, free, and private.

faqs.question: Will converting reduce the quality of my image?
faqs.answer: Conversion to lossless formats like PNG, BMP, and TIFF preserves quality. Converting to lossy formats like JPG applies compression, which trades a small amount of quality for much smaller file sizes.

faqs.question: Can I convert multiple images at once?
faqs.answer: You can convert images one at a time. Each conversion is instant and requires no waiting or upload, so converting several files is just a matter of repeating the two steps.

intro.title: What Is the Image Format Converter?
paragraphs: The Image Format Converter changes an image from one format to another — JPG to PNG, PNG to WebP, HEIC to JPG, SVG to PNG, and 20+ other combinations — in a single click. It's the fastest way to make an image compatible with a website, app, or platform.
Conversion runs locally in your browser, so images are never uploaded and the tool works instantly with no signup or cost.

sections.title: How to Convert an Image
items: Upload or drop an image.
Choose the target format and adjust the quality slider.
Click Convert, then preview the result.
Download the converted file.

sections.title: Which Format Should I Use?
paragraphs: Use JPEG for photos on the web, PNG for graphics with transparency or sharp text, WebP for the best modern web compression, SVG for scalable logos and icons, HEIC only if your target platform supports Apple's format, and ICO for Windows icons. When in doubt, PNG and WebP are safe, widely supported choices.

sections.title: Lossless vs. Lossy Conversion
paragraphs: Converting to PNG, BMP, or TIFF is lossless — every pixel is kept. Converting to JPG applies lossy compression that discards some detail to shrink the file; the higher the compression, the smaller the file and the softer the image. Transparency is lost when converting to JPG, so export PNG or WebP if you need a transparent background.

metadata.title: Chmod Calculator
metadata.description: Calculate Unix file permissions visually using chmod

faqs.question: What is chmod?
faqs.answer: chmod is a command in Unix and Unix-like systems (such as Linux and macOS) used to change the permissions of files or directories. Permissions determine who can read, write or execute a file.

faqs.question: How do permissions work?
faqs.answer: Permissions are grouped into three classes: owner, group and others. Each class can have read (r, value 4), write (w, value 2) and execute (x, value 1) permissions. These values are added together to get the numeric representation (like 755).

faqs.question: How do I use the chmod calculator?
faqs.answer: Click the permission checkboxes to set the desired permissions for owner, group and others. The calculator shows the numeric and symbolic representations in real time.

faqs.question: What is the difference between numeric and symbolic representations?
faqs.answer: The numeric representation uses three digits (like 755), where each digit is the sum of the permission values. The symbolic representation uses letters (like rwxr-xr-x), where r means read, w means write, x means execute and - means no permission.

faqs.question: What are common permission settings?
faqs.answer: 755 (rwxr-xr-x) for directories and executable files, 644 (rw-r--r--) for regular files, 700 (rwx------) for private directories, and 600 (rw-------) for sensitive files.

faqs.question: Can I set special permissions?
faqs.answer: This calculator handles basic permissions. Special permissions (such as setuid, setgid and the sticky bit) require an additional fourth digit in the numeric representation.

intro.title: What is a Chmod Calculator?
paragraphs: A chmod calculator is a free online tool for calculating the numeric and symbolic representations of Unix file permissions. It helps you visualize permissions and generate the correct syntax for the chmod command. All calculations happen in the browser.

sections.title: How to calculate permissions
paragraphs: Click the permission checkboxes to set the desired permissions for owner, group and others. The calculator shows the numeric (like 755) and symbolic (like rwxr-xr-x) representations in real time.

sections.title: Understanding permissions
paragraphs: Permissions are grouped into three classes: owner, group and others. Each class can have read (r, value 4), write (w, value 2) and execute (x, value 1) permissions. These values are added together to get the number for each class.

sections.title: Common permission modes
items: 755 (rwxr-xr-x) - Directories and executable files
644 (rw-r--r--) - Regular files
700 (rwx------) - Private directories
600 (rw-------) - Sensitive files
777 (rwxrwxrwx) - Full permissions (use with caution)

metadata.title: Cron Expression Generator
metadata.description: Visual cron expression generator with human-readable output

faqs.question: What is a cron expression?
faqs.answer: A cron expression is a string used to schedule tasks on Unix-like systems. It consists of five fields: minute, hour, day of month, month and day of week. Each field can contain specific values, ranges, lists or wildcards.

faqs.question: How do I build a cron expression?
faqs.answer: Use the presets to quickly pick common schedules, or enter a value for each field manually. The tool shows the expression in English and displays the next run times.

faqs.question: What are the fields of a cron expression?
faqs.answer: A standard cron expression has five fields: minute (0-59), hour (0-23), day of month (1-31), month (1-12) and day of week (0-7, where both 0 and 7 are Sunday).

faqs.question: What does * mean in cron?
faqs.answer: The asterisk (*) means "every" or "all". It matches every possible value for a field, meaning the task runs at every value of that field.

faqs.question: How do I specify multiple values?
faqs.answer: Use commas to separate values (like 1,3,5), hyphens for ranges (like 1-5), or step values (like */5 meaning every 5 units).

faqs.question: Are cron expressions safe?
faqs.answer: Yes. This tool generates cron expressions locally in the browser. No data is sent to any server.

sections.title: How to build a cron expression

metadata.title: CSS Minifier
metadata.description: Minify CSS to reduce file size

faqs.question: What is CSS minification?
faqs.answer: CSS minification reduces the size of a CSS file by removing unnecessary whitespace, comments and other characters. This can improve page load speed and reduce bandwidth usage.

faqs.question: How do I minify CSS?
faqs.answer: Paste your CSS code into the input field. Click the minify button. The tool removes whitespace and comments to produce a smaller output. Copy the result or download the minified file.

faqs.question: Does minification affect CSS functionality?
faqs.answer: No. Minification only removes characters that are unnecessary for rendering. The functionality of your CSS remains unchanged. However, it may make the code harder to read or debug.

faqs.question: How much can minification reduce file size?
faqs.answer: The reduction depends on the original CSS. Files with lots of whitespace and comments can be reduced by 50-80%. Already compact CSS may see only a small reduction.

faqs.question: Is my CSS sent to a server?
faqs.answer: No. All minification happens locally in your browser. The code never leaves your device.

faqs.question: Can I minify large CSS files?
faqs.answer: Yes. Since minification happens in the browser, it can handle large CSS files. However, very large files (>50 MB) may be slow due to browser memory limits.

intro.title: What is a CSS Minifier?
paragraphs: A CSS minifier is a free online tool for reducing the size of CSS files by removing unnecessary whitespace, comments and other characters. This can improve page load speed and reduce bandwidth usage. All minification happens in the browser.

sections.title: How to minify CSS
paragraphs: Paste your CSS code into the input field. Click the minify button. The tool removes whitespace and comments to produce a smaller output. Copy the result or download the minified file.

sections.title: How minification works
paragraphs: Minification removes characters that are not needed in CSS: multiple spaces become a single space, CSS comments are removed, line breaks are removed, and values are shortened where possible.

metadata.title: Hash Generator
metadata.description: Generate MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256 and more hashes from text

faqs.question: What is a hash generator?
faqs.answer: A hash generator is a tool that converts input text into a fixed-length string. Hashes are one-way — you cannot reverse a hash back into the original text. They are used for data integrity, password storage and digital signatures.

faqs.question: Which hash algorithms are supported?
faqs.answer: The tool supports SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512. SHA-256 and SHA-512 are recommended for secure applications. SHA-1 is no longer recommended for security reasons but may be used for legacy systems.

faqs.question: How do I generate a hash?
faqs.answer: Type or paste text into the input field. Select the desired hash algorithm. The hash is generated and displayed immediately. Click copy to copy it to your clipboard.

faqs.question: Are the hashes secure?
faqs.answer: SHA-256 and SHA-512 are currently considered secure. SHA-1 has known collision vulnerabilities and should not be used for security purposes. For password hashing, use dedicated functions such as bcrypt or Argon2.

faqs.question: Can I hash files?
faqs.answer: The current version only supports text input. For file hashing, you need to read the file contents and pass them as text.

faqs.question: Is hashing safe in the browser?
faqs.answer: Yes. All hashing is done in the browser using the native Web Crypto API. No data is sent to any server.

metadata.title: HTML Entity Encoder
metadata.description: Encode and decode HTML entities in text

faqs.question: What are HTML entities?
faqs.answer: HTML entities are codes used to display reserved characters or characters that are not easy to type on a keyboard in HTML. For example, < becomes <, > becomes >, and & becomes &.

faqs.question: How do I encode HTML entities?
faqs.answer: Paste your text into the input field. Select the encode mode. The tool converts special characters into HTML entities.

faqs.question: How do I decode HTML entities?
faqs.answer: Paste text containing HTML entities into the input field. Select the decode mode. The tool converts the entities back into their original characters.

faqs.question: Why do I need to encode HTML entities?
faqs.answer: Some characters have special meaning in HTML (like < and > for tags). To display them on a page, they must be encoded as entities, otherwise the browser interprets them as HTML.

faqs.question: What is the difference between named and numeric entities?
faqs.answer: Named entities use names (like <), while numeric entities use character codes (like <). They are equivalent, but named entities are easier to read.

faqs.question: Is HTML entity encoding safe?
faqs.answer: Yes. This tool encodes and decodes HTML entities locally in the browser. No data is sent to any server.

intro.title: What is an HTML Entity Encoder/Decoder?
paragraphs: An HTML entity encoder/decoder is a free online tool for converting between characters and HTML entities. It encodes special characters as entities for safe display in HTML, or decodes entities back into their original characters. All processing happens in the browser.

sections.title: How to encode HTML entities
paragraphs: Paste your text into the input field. Select the encode mode. The tool converts characters such as <, >, &, " and ' into HTML entities.

sections.title: How to decode HTML entities
paragraphs: Paste text containing HTML entities into the input field. Select the decode mode. The tool converts entities such as <, > and & back into their original characters.

metadata.title: HTML Minifier

faqs.question: What is HTML minification?
faqs.answer: HTML minification reduces the size of an HTML file by removing unnecessary whitespace, comments and optionally inlining CSS/JavaScript. This can improve page load speed and reduce bandwidth usage.

faqs.question: How do I minify HTML?
faqs.answer: Paste your HTML code into the input field. Click the minify button. The tool removes whitespace and comments to produce a smaller output. Copy the result or download the minified file.

faqs.question: Does minification affect HTML functionality?
faqs.answer: No. Minification only removes characters that are unnecessary for rendering. The functionality and appearance of your HTML remain unchanged. However, it may make the code harder to read or debug.

faqs.question: How much can minification reduce file size?
faqs.answer: The reduction depends on the original HTML. Files with lots of whitespace and comments can be reduced by 50-80%. Already compact HTML may see only a small reduction.

faqs.question: Is my HTML sent to a server?
faqs.answer: No. All minification happens locally in your browser. The code never leaves your device.

faqs.question: Can I minify large HTML files?
faqs.answer: Yes. Since minification happens in the browser, it can handle large HTML files. However, very large files (>50 MB) may be slow due to browser memory limits.

intro.title: What is an HTML Minifier?
paragraphs: An HTML minifier is a free online tool for reducing the size of HTML files by removing unnecessary whitespace, comments and other characters. This can improve page load speed and reduce bandwidth usage. All minification happens in the browser.
